analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (last-updated date and a paragraph on shared per-file leases, mtime lag, TTL expiry) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (same-file coordination row, delta failure/recency, TTL, owned retirement). No executable code, keys, endpoints, or trust-boundary wiring changed in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant behavior described (T-041, SEC-035, TB-007, A-001): complete-checkpoint reads now take a shared per-file lease, so concurrent restores read in parallel. Writers, validation, scans and retirement are exclusive. Readers rewrite mtime only when it is at least ttlSeconds/30 stale (60 s at the 1800 s TTL) and remove a corrupt file only when sole holder. A busy corrupt file may stay indexed and fail reads until it is alone, a writer validates it, or it expires.

TTL implications: the documented design does not extend retention. The 1800 s maximum TTL stays, and the docs say raising it needs a new SEC-035 sign-off. mtime can lag the last hit by up to 60 s. The docs say whole-root TTL expiry consults the in-memory last hit, so a recently hit file survives and its hit is written as mtime. A restart scan before that sweep still ages from the old mtime, which is conservative and bounded. A documented extra case is a file that gets a hit every time under simultaneous overlap: it is retained by the in-memory check rather than by mtime, up to the sliding TTL. That is consistent with the existing sliding-TTL posture. No at-rest metadata, HMAC naming, AAD, or KEK handling changes are described.

Availability: skipping busy files in scans/retirement and lease ordering could in theory allow starvation or delayed purge. The docs say a queued exclusive request blocks later readers, and maintenance never waits. This is local DoS-level and bounded by TTL expiry. It is not demonstrably a regression from docs alone.

Remaining question for integration or a code pass: the actual code in SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift, SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDHybridCheckpointStore+ReadAttempt.swift was not supplied. It should confirm the described TTL check cannot keep expired data beyond ttlSeconds, and that the lease upgrade is race-free. The reference doc patch excerpt is also truncated. No finding is made on documentation alone.
